subject: Post-demo: MedNotebook long-window fit + recommended eval path
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@mednotebook.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: MedNotebook long-window fit + recommended eval path

Claire — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed evaluation path so we can move from discovery to an actionable pilot: 

TL;DR:
- We think your primary risk is summarization fidelity across multi-visit notes and lossiness from truncation.
- Recommended pilot: 2-week long-window eval against 500 de-identified patient records, compare Redwood-30B and Redwood-70B (quantized) with the same prompt set and scoring metrics.
- Next steps: we (Redwood) deliver a prompt-set + benchmark harness by Tue 6/1; MedNotebook provides 500 de-id records and success criteria by Fri 6/4.

What we observed in the call (notes):
- Workload shape: 60% visit sequences where context > 16k tokens; 25% shorter notes; 15% very long narrative documents (discharge summaries, entire encounter histories).
- Primary user flows: concise clinical summarization for PCP handoffs, and chronological timeline extraction for coding/qa workflows.
- Constraints: on-prem requirement for PHI (you flagged SOC2 + E-2 encryption), and expected 99.9% availability SLA for batch exports.

Model & eval recommendations (high level):
1) Models to include in the pilot: Redwood-30B (fp16), Redwood-70B-quant (8-bit/kv-friendly), and a smaller contending model for cost baseline (Redwood-13B-quant).
2) Window handling strategies to test: native long-context (64k), sliding-summary + KV cache warm-start, and chunk+stitch summarization (with overlapping 512-token stride).
3) Quality metrics: ROUGE-L, nucleus-sampled human quality score (3-clinician panel), and fidelity checks for entities/medications (precision/recall).

Attachments I’m sharing now (stubs):
- mednotebook_prompt_set_v1.json — initial prompts + negative examples for hallucination tests
- long_window_benchmarks_20270530.csv — baseline perf/latency profile from our internal tests on comparable workloads

Links & artefacts:
- Long-window benchmark doc (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-long-window-benchmarks
- HubSpot record: HS-23456

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 6/1: Redwood uploads the prompt set + benchmark harness (we'll push a small Docker-based runner for your infra team).
- Fri 6/4: MedNotebook provides 500 de-id records + pass/fail criteria (entity fidelity thresholds, summary length targets).
- Week of 6/7: Redwood runs evals in private deployment (we can run in your VPC or on our Dedicated infra depending on procurement).
- By 6/18: Delivery of comparative report: latency/cost/unit, summarization fidelity, top failure modes, and recommended production configuration.

Operational notes / risks:
- If you require air-gapped on-prem, turnaround for pilot infra will be longer (we estimate +2 weeks).
- Truncation risk: any approach that simply cuts history at 8k will drop longitudinal medication changes; we recommend KV cache warm-start + chunk overlap for entity preservation.

Please confirm the timeline and whether you prefer us to run the pilot in your VPC or as a dedicated Redwood instance (we can provide SOC2-audit artifacts either way).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Post-demo: MedNotebook long-window fit + recommended eval path

Thanks Markus — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) The 500 de-id records: can they include multi-specialty histories (yes) and do we need to strip structured metadata (no, keep structured fields for entity scoring).
2) Our infra preference: VPC deployment initially; our security team will need the SOC2 artifact and an architecture diagram. Can you provide the diagram and a short checklist for onboarding?
3) For the human quality scoring: do you have a suggestion for the clinician panel composition? We'd like someone with primary care experience and someone with inpatient charting experience.

One additional ask — our product lead, Raj (cc'd on the thread), requested we include a simple latency vs. fidelity visualization in the final report. Is that in scope?

Quick answers: we can target providing records by Fri 6/4 but may need a short call with your infra person to confirm S3 access and transfer method. Also happy to accept the pilot in our VPC.

Onward,
Claire D'Souza
Head of Product, MedNotebook
claire@mednotebook.com

Claire / team — following up with concrete items and owners so we can keep momentum:

Action items (owners / due dates):
- Redwood: deliver prompt-set + harness + onboarding checklist (Markus) — due 2027-06-01
- MedNotebook: provide 500 de-id records + structured field mapping (Claire / Raj) — due 2027-06-04
- Security: provide SOC2 package + architecture diagram (Neha) — due 2027-06-02 (Neha: attaching a short checklist inline below).
- Evaluation design: define human panel + scoring rubric (Monica -> coordinate clinician panel) — deliver rubric 2027-06-07

Neha's onboarding checklist (brief):
- Exchange of DPA/NDA signed: yes (please confirm countersign)
- VPC peering or secure SFTP options: confirm method and ingress IPs
- KMS/HSM requirement: note you flagged customer-managed keys; seek confirmation if they must be enforced for pilot
- Audit logs: we will surface call-level audit logs for all requests (retention options configurable)

On the model choices Markus suggested: we'll include Redwood-30B (fp16), Redwood-70B-quant (kv-optimized), and Redwood-13B-quant for cost baseline. We'll also run an ablation test for chunk+stitch vs. KV warm-start so we can show where entity dropoff happens.

For the latency vs fidelity visualization — yes, we can include a scatter with per-record fidelity score vs median token-latency; we'll add a cost-per-record column to the final sheet.

If this plan looks good we can schedule a short 30-min kickoff with security + infra tomorrow. Markus — can you share the docker runner link and the Drive folder once you push them?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
